transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-08-30 15:00 UTC | Duration: 46m | Attendees: Maya Chen, Diego Ramos (Redwood); Sofia Patel, Liam O'Connor, Rahul Mehta, Emily Barnes (North Harbor Foods)

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone good afternoon, thanks for carving out time. quick check — can you all hear me okay?
[00:07] Sofia Patel: Yep audible. thanks Maya.
[00:12] Maya Chen: Awesome. High level agenda — we want to align on pilot goals, get staging + VPC peering steps clarified, and cover security asks so we can get you into a canary by the second week of September. Diego's going to walk the runtime checklist.
[00:27] Diego Ramos: Hi, hi. I'll keep it practical, not too deep today. we'll go over env requirements, tokenization expectations, and a small perf plan for your summarization and support use cases.
[00:40] Liam O'Connor: Quick note from infra — we prefer VPC peering for now, not transit gateways. also curious about IP ranges and if Redwood needs a static egress.
[00:50] Maya Chen: Good call. For hosted dedicated we can do peering, we have an egress IP option but it's a paid add-on, I can include that in the doc.
[01:00] Rahul Mehta: On security — SOC2 is a must for our procurement, also want to understand key management, KMS/HSM integration, and retention for logs. are audit logs exported?
[01:14] Diego Ramos: Yes, we have audit logs, you can stream to your SIEM. small caveat — some events are batched, so timestamps may lag a few seconds, but full provenance is retained.
[01:28] Emily Barnes: Our pilot success criteria: 1) mean latency under 250ms P95 for support chat paths, 2) order summarization accuracy above 92% on our eval set, and 3) predictable cost under $0.015 per 1k tokens — approximate.
[01:48] Maya Chen: Great explicit metrics, helpful. we'll validate latency with a perf run and provide model/quantization recommendations to meet the cost target.
[02:00] Diego Ramos: For the perf plan — two parts: one synthetic load to validate P95 under expected concurrency, and one small production-like canary with sampled traffic. we'll instrument prefix/K-V cache (sometimes transcribed as K-V cash) and batching to hit latency/cost targets.
[02:20] Liam O'Connor: How invasive is the KV cache? does that require syncing?
[02:25] Diego Ramos: No external sync, it's internal to the runtime. we expose hints for cache keys, but nothing you need to manage. apologies if earlier docs said KV cache, sometimes the audio spells it out as K-V cash in transcripts, ha.
[02:41] Sofia Patel: Can you give an ops checklist for staging — what do we need to open on our side?
[02:46] Maya Chen: Sure, quick list: CIDR for peering, IAM role or cert for access, list of test prompts/evals, and a security contact to review SOC2 artifacts. i'll send a formal staging checklist after the call.
[02:58] Rahul Mehta: On KMS — does Redwood integrate with external cloud KMS or is key management within Redwood?
[03:05] Diego Ramos: We support customer-managed keys via most cloud KMS providers and we also offer bring-your-own-key for Private deployments. For hosted, CMK via your cloud is supported when you opt into the package.
[03:18] Maya Chen: We'll attach our SOC2 and an SAML/SSO runbook. Side note: procurement teams sometimes ask for an IP allowlist, we'll show the egress IPs if you choose that add-on.
[03:30] Emily Barnes: Procurement will want that yes.
[03:33] Maya Chen: Okay. Next — timeline. can we aim to have peering and staging creds by 2026-09-01?
[03:42] Liam O'Connor: yes that's realistic. i can create the peering and share details by then.
[03:46] Maya Chen: perfect. Diego, can you outline the quick bench steps now?
[03:50] Diego Ramos: Sure. Step 1: we deploy a small runner in your staging with our runtime and a pinned model. Step 2: run synthetic tokens to simulate peak concurrency — we suggested sample traffic of ~120 concurrent users for 60s. Step 3: run a 1-hour canary with sampled real traffic, collect token costs and latency. we'll produce a short report and change recs.
[04:20] Sofia Patel: For the eval set, we'll share our order summarization test cases (about 400 examples). any format constraints?
[04:28] Diego Ramos: CSV or JSONL is fine, just include prompt/context and expected output. we'll wire them into our eval harness.
[04:36] Maya Chen: we'll also map features to Redwood Console for observability — you'll get token-level breakdowns and per-route latency.
[04:44] Rahul Mehta: A couple security edge cases — do logs contain PII? we need to know redaction policies.
[04:52] Diego Ramos: By default logs are redacted for PII markers, we can also enable additional redaction rules. for Private deployments you keep logs in your VPC if needed.
[05:05] Speaker 1: (mutter) is there an SLA for dedicated?
[05:08] Maya Chen: Dedicated has SLA options, i'll include the tiers.
[05:12] Emily Barnes: also curious about rollout policy — can we A/B test model variants?
[05:16] Diego Ramos: Absolutely, Console supports canary and A/B rollouts, and automatic fallback to cheaper model variant if throughput gets constrained. we'll demonstrate in a follow-up demo.
[05:30] Maya Chen: Ok let's recap action items — i'll send the onboarding runbook and staging checklist, Diego will draft bench plan, Liam will create peering, Rahul will review SOC2. any other blockers?
[05:42] Sofia Patel: Not from product side. main blocker is procurement review timeline.
[05:47] Maya Chen: Understood, include procurement in the SOC2 review thread. we'll try to compress responses to help stay on time.
[05:56] Liam O'Connor: another tiny detail — do you need specific NAT/gateway settings for peering?
[06:01] Diego Ramos: No special NAT, just standard route tables and security groups. we'll provide an example snippet in the checklist.
[06:10] Emily Barnes: Great. looking forward to the perf run.
[06:13] Maya Chen: we'll target the week of 2026-09-06 for the perf/canary run and i'll email calendar invites once we lock times. thanks everyone, ending a little early, appreciate it.

Post-meeting notes: shared links referenced during call: onboarding runbook (link: https://redwood.example.com/runbook/nhf-onboard) — staging checklist (attached), SOC2 packet (link), sample bench spreadsheet (link). Some transcription errors present: vendor names occasionally misheard, and internal acronyms like KV cache were rendered as K-V cash.

End of transcript.
